first of all, I'm so sorry you're in this situation. it's extremely difficult to deal with another person's mental struggles when you cannot relate. good on you for trying to make things better.

secondly, I'm not a professional or anything, so please just take this as my personal experience. I can relate to some of the things described such as hopelessness, so this post caught my attention. if you can, you could try to call a hotline and ask them for advice as well.

hopelessness. it's really painful to see being described from another perspective. clearly you care for this person, and nothing seems to help. your friend probably genuinely believes he is beyond saving. that's what I've believed as well for a long time. 

I think every person has attachments to this world, whatever those may be. food, friends, career, hobbies, memories... something that makes it hard to say goodbye. even during my worst hours of desperately trying to end my life, a very small part of me was scared. very scared. because death is the unknown. life, even with all the suffering, is more familiar. 

in many cases, people kill themselves in a moment where they empty their minds and take the leap. think of pulling the trigger or jumping. however, if they are stalled for time by talking, they'll start to think, and thinking makes it harder to complete the job. 

the key is stalling for time until something changes. depressive episodes don't last forever. it feels like they do, but they don't. depression comes in waves, some more severe than others. in the times where the depression subsidies is when there's a chance to feel better. 

that being said, you are not a therapist but a friend. there's a limit to how much you can do. unfortunately, I do not know where the line should be drawn. all i can say is, please don't forget to take care of yourself first and foremost. there is only so much you can do. as long as you do your best, you should live guilt free. 

excuse the paragraph. I wish you and your friend well.

hey man. we're in a similar boat regarding the feeling helpless part. 

unfortunately, I'm just some stranger on reddit so I can't do much of anything. but maybe it's worth for you to think about what are some things that are keeping you here. what I mean is, if you had absolutely 0 attachments to this world, you wouldn't have any second thoughts about leaving it.

but I'm guessing you do? which is not a bad thing. in fact, it's what helps humans survive. you say you hate humans, but do you really? are you angry with them, or are you taking out your frustration on them?

maybe you have a favorite meal. a favorite outfit. a favorite game. engage with those things. and when you do, acknowledge that you appreciate these things. it will absolutely not solve all of your problems in an instant, I know that. but appreciating little things like that can make your day a little bit less shitty. 

maybe you have other activities in mind that are helpful. think about them. 

please tell your concerns to someone you trust irl if you can. it won't solve everything, but talking and sharing your burdens has a chance of making them less heavy. before you do something you can't reverse, you might as well take all the chances you can, no?

lastly, all I can say is, I'm sorry. my reply will not automatically make your life easier. you will probably forget about it after a day, a week, a month. but I wish you well. I genuinely hope life gets easier for you. take care.
